subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification / GPU types & throughput targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@storix.ai>, Ben Harris <ben.harris@storix.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: dedicated capacity sizing & pricing next steps

Hi Samantha / Ben  great to speak earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we’re aligned: 

What we covered
- Use case: Storix will run multi-turn assistant for customer support + on-demand summaries. Typical request size ~4080 tokens; some longer summary jobs up to 512 tokens.
- Traffic shape: you said steady daytime traffic with 12x peak bursts; ballpark of 35M tokens/day (90150M tokens/month) for initial launch, with growth to ~10M tokens/day in 612 months.
- Performance target: p50 latency <300ms for short-turn prompts; support bursts up to ~35k concurrent requests.
- Procurement/budget: you flagged an initial budget band of $10k$20k/month.

Open questions we committed to follow up on
1) Which GPU family makes the most sense given your mix of short prompts + occasional long summaries (A100 80GB vs H100)?
2) Reserved capacity sizing: how many GPUs to reserve initially vs. planned scale cadence.
3) Target unit economics (target $/1M tokens) so we can map to a draft Dedicated quote.

Attached: capacity_estimates.xlsx  a quick worksheet I used on the call to map tokens/day -> rough throughput and GPU counts.

Next steps
- I’ll follow up with two configuration options (small / initial and recommended growth) plus ballpark monthly pricing and unit-costs per 1M tokens based on your 90150M/mo range.
- Can you confirm: average tokens per prompt (short path) and percent of requests that are long summaries (>256 tokens)? That will change the GPU recommendation.
- If that looks OK, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with Marcus (infrastructure) to validate latency SLOs and run a small perf pilot.

Thanks  talk soon.
—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa  super helpful recap. A few clarifications / answers below: 

Traffic details (closer estimate)
- Expected steady state for launch: 4M tokens/day ( 120M/month).
- Avg tokens per short prompt: ~55 tokens.
- Long summaries (>256 tokens): ~810% of requests, avg summary ~400 tokens.
- Peak bursts: up to ~2.5x baseline for short windows during product updates.

Budget & targets
- Procurement is comfortable evaluating in the $10k$20k/month band for the initial committed term.
- We'd like to aim for unit economics < $100 per 1M tokens if possible (higher is tolerable short-term if performance needs it).

Questions for Redwood
1) Given the mix above, do you recommend starting on A100 80GB or H100? We care about latency for short prompts but also memory headroom for long summaries and larger context.
2) What reserved capacity would you recommend to safely handle steady 4M/day with 2.5x burst and that long-summary mix?
3) Can you provide a draft SOW/quote we can share with procurement?

Happy to hop on a quick 30-min technical follow-up next week with Marcus and your infra team.

Thanks for the details, Samantha  this is perfect and very helpful. Attached is a ballpark quote and two configuration options (redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.pdf). Below are distilled recommendations and the assumptions I used so procurement has context.

Assumptions we used for the math
- Baseline tokens: 4M/day (~120M/month).
- Long summaries are 10% of requests (~400 tokens each).
- Average request size (blended): ~70 tokens.
- Target unit economics you called out: < $100 per 1M tokens for procurement sensitivity.

Recommended starting configs (ballpark):
1) Option A  Cost-conscious starter (2x A100 80GB reserved)
- Throughput profile: steady-state support for ~3.5k6k tokens/sec (handles 4M/day with 2.5x burst for short-turns; long summaries will increase latency under heavy burst).
- Use cases: best if most traffic is short-turn prompts and you can tolerate slightly higher p95 latency during long-summary spikes.
- Ballpark committed price: $9,000$12,000 / month (Redwood-managed Dedicated pool, includes baseline support & monitoring).
- Implied unit-cost (given 120M/mo): ~$75$100 per 1M tokens (ballpark).

2) Option B  Performance & headroom (2x H100 equivalents or 4x A100 80GB reserved)
- Throughput profile: steady-state 8k15k tokens/sec, much better headroom for long summaries and higher concurrency; p50/p95 latency targets hold under heavier bursts.
- Use cases: recommended if you expect to ramp quickly to ~10M tokens/day or need consistent low p95 for mixed-length workloads.
- Ballpark committed price: $20,000$26,000 / month.
- Implied unit-cost (given 120M/mo): ~$160$216 per 1M tokens (note: higher per-1M if you under-utilize capacity; unit-cost improves as you consume more tokens).

Notes on GPU family
- A100 80GB: great balance for short-turn heavy workloads with occasional long summaries. Good memory for ~400 token sequences, lower cost than H100.
- H100: better perf for large-batch or long-context models, and for some newer model variants; higher cost but more headroom and better latency at high concurrency for those workloads.

What I recommend
- Start with Option A (2x A100) if you want to stay inside the $10k$20k band for procurement and validate traffic. We can set autoscaling/burst policies and a short pilot so you can measure actual utilization; after 3060 days we can revisit and size to Option B if needed.
- If procurement needs a sub-$100 per 1M tokens target, we’ll need to lock a longer committed term or a higher committed token volume to bring the implied unit-cost down  I’ll call this out in the formal quote.

Next steps
- I’ve attached a draft quote (redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.pdf) and an assumptions worksheet.
- Marcus / Dev  can we schedule a 30-min infra deep-dive this week to validate latency SLOs and confirm the perf pilot runbook? I’ll set a meeting once Samantha confirms availability.
- Samantha / Ben  if you’re comfortable I’ll mark up the SOW with a 60-day pilot option and a procurement-friendly payment schedule.

Thanks  looking forward to next steps.
—
